elements.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Rendered 6.1 replaces the covenant with "The Company may participate in any project on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or any other products, and may use and license the 'Deerskin' brand, without restriction under this Agreement." Both the prohibition on participating in similar Internet projects (an open-ended field-of-use/competing-products restriction) and HDI's exclusive right to the Customer's own "Deerskin" brand are removed, so no Vendor exclusivity survives to block Customer use of its own product or brand; deterministic check "no open-ended compete restriction on Customer remains" is ok.

elements.element: The restriction covers only a named competing product.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: after the redline no restriction on Customer's competing activity exists in 6.1, so there is no scope to narrow to a named product.

elements.element: The restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: the deleted covenant's "during the term of this Agreement" trigger is gone along with the covenant; no post-term or in-term restriction remains.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: no duration runs because no restriction survives (the auto-renewal concern under Section 4.1 is moot once the covenant is deleted).

elements.element: The restriction permits Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: the affirmative language expressly allows participation in "any project on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or any other products", so internal development is unimpeded.
Vacuously satisfied: no covenant remains that could reach acquired businesses or products.

reasons: Preferred level is position-complete: the single preferred element is met in operative text, not merely promised in the comment; the fallback offer is confined to the margin comment where it belongs.

Deleting HDI's exclusive right to the "Deerskin" brand was necessary, not an extra: an exclusive Vendor right over Customer's own brand is itself a field-of-use restriction, and the preferred result would be incomplete while it stood.

Minimality holds: the edit is confined to Section 6.1, the concise affirmative replacement adds no new obligations, procedures, survival tails or damages language, and HDI's own exclusivity covenant (6.3) and Customer's closeout carve-out (6.2) are retained untouched.

The removed lead-in "Except as provided in Section 6.2" was an exception to the deleted restriction only; Section 6.2 remains operative on its own terms, so no dangling cross-reference or undefined term is created.

Drafting caution (not a failure on the record before me): the phrase "without restriction under this Agreement" is broader than needed and, if any unrelated retained provision (e.g. confidentiality, Site-related obligations, or IP licence limits) constrains Customer's use of the brand or products, it could read as an override. If you want to remove that risk without changing the outcome, narrow to "The Company is subject to no non-compete or field-of-use restriction under this Agreement, and may use and license the 'Deerskin' brand."
